description: pkix-path/src/lib.rs §6.1.5(g) cascade deletion (line 2357): 'for d in 2..=leaf_depth'. The vpns nodes (which were deleted at depth=vpns_depth) are at depth >= 1. Their children start at depth+1. If vpns nodes are at depth 1, their children at depth 2 are handled by d=2. But the tree.retain for to_delete_vpns (line 2350) handles vpns nodes themselves. After deleting vpns nodes, the cascade starts at d=2 to clean up children of deleted vpns nodes. This looks correct for the case where vpns nodes are at depth 1. BUT: the comment says vpns nodes are 'nodes whose parent has valid_policy == anyPolicy' — for deeper trees, vpns nodes can be at depth > 1 (if there are intermediate anyPolicy nodes). For a 3-cert chain with anyPolicy at depth 2, vpns nodes are at depth 3 (leaf). The cascade for their children would start at d=4 which is leaf_depth+1 — out of range, no iteration. This case (leaf-depth vpns) is correctly handled: no children exist at leaf_depth+1 so there's nothing to cascade-delete. Verify this edge case with a deeper test chain.
notes: FALSE POSITIVE after deeper analysis. The cascade 'for d in 2..=leaf_depth' is a general sweep that correctly propagates deletions from any depth. It doesn't need to know the depth of the vpns nodes - it sweeps all depths from 2 to leaf_depth, removing any node whose parent no longer exists. This correctly handles vpns nodes at any depth. Closing.
title: §6.1.5(g) cascade deletion only starts at d=2, skipping depth-1 vpns children cleanup
